title: The 'Clean Enough' Weekly Reset: A Checklist for Messy Brains
description: A 45-minute weekly home reset checklist for ADHD brains, split into 3 short rounds so you can stop anytime and still win.
intro:
"Sunday reset" videos are everywhere: fresh sheets, spotless kitchen, a perfectly planned week, and it all looks very peaceful. Meanwhile we're at 4pm on Sunday, staring at the laundry pile and wondering where the weekend went.

Here's a version of the weekly reset that fits our brains. It's split into three short rounds of about 15 minutes each. You can do one, two or all three. Each round leaves the house better than before.

The goal isn't perfect. The goal is *clean enough to start Monday without dread.*

sections.heading: Before you start: 2-minute setup
sections.body:
Grab your caddy, a trash bag, a laundry basket for "elsewhere" stuff and a visual timer. Put on a playlist or a podcast.

Tell yourself (out loud if it helps): "I'm doing Round 1. That's it. Anything else is bonus."

sections.heading: Round 1: Reset the surfaces (15 minutes)
sections.body:
This round gives the most visual win for the least effort.

- [ ] Walk through with a trash bag. Grab obvious trash.
- [ ] Carry dishes to the kitchen.
- [ ] Clear the kitchen counters.
- [ ] Clear the coffee table and dining table.
- [ ] Toss "elsewhere" stuff into the basket.
- [ ] Wipe the counters and table.

When the timer goes off, stop and look around. The house already looks different, and your brain gets a hit of "oh, nice."

sections.heading: Round 2: Reset the systems (15 minutes)
sections.body:
This round is about the things that make next week run smoother.

- [ ] Start a load of laundry (set a timer to move it).
- [ ] Empty the launch pad tray and check the outgoing bin.
- [ ] Go through the mail and paper pocket.
- [ ] Take out all trash and recycling.
- [ ] Walk the "elsewhere" basket around and drop things in their rooms.
- [ ] Put fresh towels in the bathroom.

sections.heading: Round 3: Reset for Monday (15 minutes)
sections.body:
This one is for future-you.

- [ ] Look at the calendar for the week. Write it on the command center.
- [ ] Make a quick meal plan (even 3 dinners count).
- [ ] Start the grocery list.
- [ ] Charge devices, set out bags and keys.
- [ ] Pick out Monday's outfit.
- [ ] Do one kind thing for yourself: fresh sheets, a candle, a clean water bottle.

sections.heading: If you only have 5 minutes
sections.body:
Some weeks, even 15 minutes feels like too much. That's okay. Here's the micro version:

1. Trash out.
2. Dishes in the sink or dishwasher.
3. Look at tomorrow on the calendar.

Five minutes, three things. You've still done a reset, and Monday-you will still notice the difference. The micro version exists so that a hard week never turns into zero. Zero is what makes the next week feel impossible, and one tiny step keeps the door open.

sections.heading: What's NOT on the list
sections.body:
Deep cleaning. Organizing closets. Scrubbing grout. Baseboards.

Those are bonus projects for a day you have extra energy. The weekly reset is about keeping the house *functional*, not about fixing everything. Mixing the two is how a reset turns into an all-day project that you avoid next week.

sections.heading: Tips to make it stick
sections.body:
- **Same time every week.** Sunday afternoon, Saturday morning or Friday night. The time matters less than it being consistent.
- **Invite the household.** Everyone takes a round, or everyone takes a room.
- **Reward yourself.** Coffee, a show, a walk. Your brain works better with a carrot.
- **Skip the guilt.** Missed a week? Do Round 1 today. Rounds 2 and 3 can wait.

sections.heading: Make it visual
sections.body: Checklists work best when you can see them and check things off by hand. Tape your list inside a cabinet door or put it in a sheet protector on the fridge and use a dry-erase marker. Checking boxes is weirdly satisfying, and satisfying is exactly what keeps us coming back.

finds.name: Magnetic dry-erase checklist
finds.why: Write your routine once, check it off daily, wipe it clean. No app to forget.

finds.name: Visual countdown timer
finds.search: visual countdown timer for kids and adults
finds.why: A shrinking color disk shows how much time is left, so "a few minutes" becomes real.

outro:
Three rounds, 15 minutes each, and permission to stop after any of them. That's a weekly reset that works on real weekends.

Want this checklist ready to print? It's page one of the *Tidy Brain Printable Pack*, along with daily and room-by-room lists.
